title: The Penguin Who Just Stands There

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — NATURE, ECOLOGY AND ANIMALS (NAT-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Isola's animals, plants, tides and weather: tide pools and nesting beaches, washed-up rubbish, shrinking clam beds, strange visitors, creatures doing what creatures do, and choices about the island where nobody gets a perfect answer.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a child aged 5-13)

collection.description: A scruffy penguin has stood on the far beach for three days, and a child is worried: explain what is happening, or bring a fish.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A penguin has turned up on the far beach. This happens once in a long, long while, and nobody quite knows why: they come from somewhere colder, on currents nobody can see. This one is scruffy, with feathers coming out in tufts, and it has been standing in the same spot for three days without moving. (friend) is worried sick. (subject) has heard about this from the oldest fishers.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "It's changing its feathers," (subject) says. "All of them at once. It can't swim until the new ones are in, so it just stands there and waits." (friend) wants to feed it. (subject) says the old fishers say it's best to leave it be, and keep the dogs away. (friend) appoints (friend.him/her)self Penguin Guard. Every day for two weeks (friend.he/she) sits a respectful distance away. Then one morning, sleek and new, the penguin waddles into the sea and is gone.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) can't bear it and leaves a small fish near the penguin. The penguin looks at the fish. It looks at (friend). It goes back to looking at the sea. The fish is eaten by a gull. (subject) puts an arm round (friend). "Some creatures just need waiting for," (subject.he/she) says. The penguin does leave, eventually, looking much smarter than when it came. (friend) claims a little of the credit.
